title: Falafel
subtitle: Crisp deep-fried chickpea fritters
excerpt: Crisp, golden deep-fried patties of soaked chickpeas blended with herbs and spices. Light and fluffy inside, crunchy outside. Served with tahini sauce and flatbread.

recipe.sourceNotes: Falafel is one of the most widely eaten street foods in the Middle East and has been a staple food in Egypt, the Levant, and beyond for centuries. The Egyptian version (ta'amiya) uses dried broad beans; the Levantine version uses chickpeas. The critical technique that distinguishes good falafel from dense, dry patties is the use of dried chickpeas soaked overnight (not tinned or cooked chickpeas). Dried chickpeas that have been soaked but not cooked produce a lighter, more open crumb after frying because the starch in the chickpea has not already been gelatinised by cooking. Using tinned chickpeas produces dense, heavy falafel that falls apart in the oil. The mixture must be processed to a coarse paste, not a smooth one: texture is essential. Falafel is traditionally deep-fried but can be shallow-fried or baked (the texture and flavour are inferior but acceptable).

recipeTools.notes: A deep, heavy saucepan for frying. A thermometer for the oil.

content.text: Use dried chickpeas soaked overnight in cold water, not tinned. The chickpeas must not be cooked: they are blended raw after soaking. This is the critical step that produces light, fluffy falafel. The mixture should be a slightly rough, grainy paste: do not over-process. If the mixture feels wet or sticky, refrigerate it for 30 minutes before shaping. Fry at 175 C: if the oil is too cool the falafel absorb oil and become greasy; if too hot the outside burns before the inside cooks.

items.preparation: soaked overnight in cold water; drained; NOT cooked

content.text: Drain the soaked chickpeas thoroughly. Put the chickpeas, onion, garlic, parsley, coriander, spices, baking powder, and salt in a food processor. Pulse to a coarse, slightly rough paste: do not over-blend to a smooth puree. Refrigerate for 20 minutes.
Heat the oil in a deep saucepan to 175 C. Shape the mixture into small patties or balls. Fry in batches of 5 to 6 for 3 to 4 minutes, turning once, until deep golden-brown. Drain on kitchen paper.
Make the tahini sauce: whisk the tahini with the lemon juice and enough cold water to make a pourable sauce. Season with salt. Serve the falafel immediately with the tahini sauce and warm flatbread.
